clue.text: Pay for tea, dipping into resources

indicators.note: tea dipping into something sits inside it, so the word for tea goes within the word for resources

parts.note: a purse is one's funds or resources
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: Someone pays for their cup of tea out of their own pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: To buy something is to pay for it, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: Oppressive temperature in chamber

parts.note: close weather is humid and oppressive

explanation.surface: A room is stiflingly hot.
explanation.definitionFit: A small private room or cupboard is a chamber in the older sense of the word.

clue.text: Republican's quitting a good deal further behind

indicators.note: a Republican quitting leaves the longer word without that letter

parts.note: a raft of things is a great many of them
R is the abbreviation for Republican; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A Republican walks out of a negotiation and so falls further behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a good deal' reads as a bargain but means a large amount, RAFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical term for the rear of a ship, so towards the back, further behind.

clue.text: Retreating in disarray, some ultimately join up again

indicators.note: something in disarray is jumbled, so these letters are rearranged
ultimately points to the final letter of the word some

explanation.surface: Retreating troops in disorder regroup, some at least.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in disarray' turns RETREATING into REINTEGRAT; the last letter of 'some' adds the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: To reintegrate is to bring parts back together, to reunite into a whole.

clue.text: List of exam scores, perhaps, English included, worth promoting?

indicators.note: English included means its letter is placed within the table

parts.note: a mark table would list exam scores, perhaps

explanation.surface: A school's league table of results is used for publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: Something marketable is saleable, so worth advertising and promoting; the question mark admits the looseness.

clue.text: Enthusiasm prize student's full of

indicators.note: the phrase is full of the answer, which lies inside the run of letters

explanation.surface: A star pupil is brimming with keenness.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest is gusto, eager enjoyment, a close synonym of enthusiasm.

clue.text: Journalist on hill brought down

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: a fell is a hill, especially in northern England
ED, editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter was knocked down on a hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: Felled means cut or knocked down, as trees or an opponent are.

clue.text: Devoted nurses going too far to dance

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: devoted, as in gave time or effort
OTT is over the top, going too far

explanation.surface: Devoted carers take things to excess in order to dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The gavotte is an old French dance in moderate time.

clue.text: Fruit spirit in pot without lid knocked over

indicators.note: one piece in another sits inside it
a pot knocked over is upside down, so its letters run backwards
a lid is the top, so the first letter of pot goes

parts.note: an angel is a heavenly spirit

explanation.surface: A drinker sees a spirit in a lidless pot that has been tipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without lid' leaves OT from POT, and 'knocked over' turns it to TO, which holds ANGEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a citrus fruit, a hybrid of tangerine and pomelo.

clue.text: Short bar put out

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A brief pub scene: the bar is shut.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrupt can mean curt or short in manner.

clue.text: Web-hosted vote's succeeding

indicators.note: the web hosting means the vote sits inside the word for the web

parts.note: the net is the World Wide Web
X is the mark made on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: An online ballot is a success.
explanation.definitionFit: Next means following on, coming after, as succeeding does.

clue.text: Crooked mat, they say, for a corner

indicators.note: they say signals that the words are heard, a sound-alike

parts.note: crooked is wry and a mat is a tangle, as of hair

explanation.surface: A rug lying askew is set right in the corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A corner of a square is a ninety-degree turn, so a corner is an example.

clue.text: Queen wearing shapeless minidress gets chilly reception

indicators.note: the Queen wearing a garment is inside it

parts.note: a shift is a loose shapeless dress, and a mini one is short
R is Regina, queen

explanation.surface: A monarch in a skimpy frock is coldly received.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for curt dismissive treatment, a frosty welcome.

clue.text: The lady closing gates with haste

indicators.note: closing letters are the last letters of each word

explanation.surface: A woman hurriedly shuts the gates.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun for a woman already mentioned, the lady in question.

clue.text: Rejected noodle: go for baked food

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: a noodle and a sap are both fools
a go is a try

explanation.surface: A diner sends back a noodle and tries a baked dish instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noodle' looks like pasta but means a fool, SAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastry is dough that is baked, as in pies and tarts.

clue.text: Cashed in, as each new driver is apparently overdrawn?

indicators.note: the pieces are apparently in the red, so they are placed inside the word for overdrawn

parts.note: an overdrawn account is in the red
L is the learner plate shown by a new driver
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newly qualified driver has spent so much the bank account is overdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: An overdrawn account is said to be 'in the red'; 'apparently' marks that idiom as the container signal, and 'as' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise an asset is to sell it for cash, to cash it in.

clue.text: Vital fluid — granny given litre infusion?

indicators.note: an infusion puts one thing into another, so the litre goes inside

parts.note: a granny is father's mother, pa's ma

explanation.surface: A grandmother is put on a drip.
explanation.walkthrough: Granny is PA'S MA, written PASMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Plasma is the liquid part of blood, a vital fluid.

clue.text: He's stopped working on island

parts.note: re means on or about
Tiree is an island of the Inner Hebrides, in Scotland

explanation.surface: A man has given up work and lives on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: One who has stopped working is by definition a pensioner who has left employment.

clue.text: Terse report on 21's bloodsuckers

definitions.meaning: 21 is the winged horse of myth, so the shortest account of it is two words: the animal and what it does
biting insects that feed on blood

explanation.walkthrough: 21 is PEGASUS, the winged horse: the briefest report on it is HORSE FLIES.
explanation.definitionFit: These large biting flies suck the blood of livestock and people.

clue.text: Suggestions drawn up with European attention to formality?

indicators.note: in a down clue drawn up means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: tips are suggestions
and means with
a Pole is a European, Polish the adjective

explanation.surface: Proposals are written up by someone from Europe with an eye for protocol.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for meticulous smartness and ceremony, as in military parade shine.

clue.text: Long-established toy on offer originally

parts.note: on is the leg side in cricket

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of offer

explanation.surface: A classic toy is on sale for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is also called the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: These interlocking plastic bricks have been a toy for decades.

clue.text: Spring holiday with least to offer?

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
a rest is a break or holiday

explanation.surface: A spring break is a sparse affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparest means most meagre, having the least to give.

clue.text: Pedant regularly blocking taxes for covenants

indicators.note: blocking means sitting in the middle of the other word

parts.note: to tax someone's patience is to try it

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of pedant

explanation.surface: A pedant obstructs tax laws written into agreements.
explanation.definitionFit: Treaties are formal agreements, which covenants also are.

clue.text: Eg. help writer with a mobile phone supplier?

indicators.note: mobile means moving about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Helping a writer get a mobile phone.
explanation.definitionFit: Early telephone lines ran over these wires, so they supplied a phone connection.

clue.text: Extra staff set up permitted household fitting

parts.note: over means extra, left over
to man is to staff

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means placed upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: let means permitted

explanation.surface: Additional staff are allowed to install fixtures.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelf or ornamental structure above a fireplace, fitted in a house.

clue.text: Holds water, taking firm position to drink

parts.note: a stand is a firm position, as in take a stand
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone takes a stand and has a drink of water.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument that holds water is sound and survives scrutiny.

clue.text: Harmful beast one's restrained by common sense

indicators.note: the beast restrained by the sense word is held inside it

parts.note: nous is common sense
an ox is a beast
I is one; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A dangerous animal is held back by sensible people.
explanation.definitionFit: Noxious means harmful or poisonous.

clue.text: Stallion keeps steady, crossing America northwards

indicators.note: crossing means placed inside, so one goes into the other

parts.note: pegs holds things in place, keeping them steady

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: USA is America

explanation.surface: A horse is tethered while it travels north through America.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged horse of Greek myth is a stallion.

clue.text: Cutting base, man needs large saw

indicators.note: cutting into a word sits inside it

parts.note: a bed is a base, as a seabed
he is a man

explanation.surface: A man trims a base and needs a large saw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like a tool but is the past of see.
explanation.definitionFit: Beheld is the past tense of behold, to see.

clue.text: Where most inmates have time to get a move on

definitions.meaning: slang for prison, where prisoners do time
to start moving, as in to rouse oneself

explanation.definitionFit: Slang term for jail, and also a verb meaning to start moving.
